data.gender_notes: Kamu is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Kamu is the name of the goddess of desire, beauty, and sexuality. She is also known as Rati, the wife of the god of love, Kamadeva. In Hindu mythology, Kamu is depicted as a beautiful woman with a red body, four arms, and adorned with precious gems and flowers. The name Kamu carries the meaning “Goddess of desire, beauty” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kamu usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of desire, beauty and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes desire for knowledge, spiritual growth, and inner beauty.

data.cultural_impact: Kamu represents the divine aspect of human desires, particularly the desires for love, beauty, and sexuality. In Hindu culture, these desires are not considered negative but rather natural and essential aspects of human life. Kamu is worshipped as a goddess to fulfill these desires and to bring harmony and balance in one's life.
data.spiritual_significance: Kamu is a symbol of the divine feminine and the power of attraction and love. She represents the deeper spiritual need for connection, intimacy, and beauty in our lives. Worshipping Kamu can help individuals cultivate a healthier and more balanced approach to their desires, and foster a deeper understanding of the crucial role that love and beauty play in our spiritual journey.
